title: Build the first psychiatry medication identity allowlist
proposedRouting: Use the exact RxNorm Current Prescribable Content release for identity only, then curate a board-relevant psychiatry ingredient allowlist before any formulation, class, indication, safety, fit, formulary, case, or point behavior is added.
guidance: The user selected a psychiatry-first rather than all-U.S.-products approach. Start with common antidepressants, mood stabilizers, antipsychotics, anxiolytics, medications for common adverse effects, sleep, ADHD, and substance-use treatment. The current gap audit suggests an initial identity review that includes paroxetine, fluvoxamine, venlafaxine, desvenlafaxine, duloxetine, trazodone, lamotrigine, carbamazepine, risperidone, paliperidone, clozapine, ziprasidone, lurasidone, cariprazine, lorazepam, clonazepam, diazepam, hydroxyzine, prazosin, and benztropine. This is a proposed review list, not a recommendation, formulary, or authorization to bulk import. Resolve ingredient-versus-product granularity one decision at a time and keep aliases/RxCUIs out of the free-text class field.
resurfacingTrigger: Before implementing an RxNorm importer or adding more runtime medication definitions.

title: Audit the current medication tags and fit rules
proposedRouting: Inventory each current class/tag, author override, and active fit modifier; connect exact claims to formal contributions or preserve them as concise Developer opinion, then review clinical direction separately from game-point magnitude.
guidance: The current thirteen compatibility files are sufficient for the prototype but are not a sourced template for scale. Free-text class and mechanism/safety tags, plus active bupropion and mirtazapine fit concepts, need claim-level provenance. RxNorm can normalize identity but cannot support first-line status, contraindications, interactions, monitoring, comparative fit, or point values. Create smaller source requests by exact claim when the existing evidence catalog does not answer it.
resurfacingTrigger: When a medication tag or modifier is promoted, changed, or used to generate additional patients.

title: Use stable therapy-modality identities without encounter fidelity mechanics
proposedRouting: Use one stable file and ID per selectable modality. Preserve delivery- or course-specific wording in source contributions and condition dossiers, but compile encounter treatment selection and scoring to the intervention ID only.
guidance: A selected psychotherapy is a recommendation of that modality now, analogous to selecting a medication without simulating a future adequate trial. Do not add duration, session count, protocol fidelity, practitioner, completion, or full-program fields to encounter treatment state. Source and condition records may retain scoped statements such as a recommendation for a full course of DBT, but the focused encounter compiler projects that statement to intervention.psychotherapy.dbt. Keep efficacy, combination, redundancy, capability, provenance, and point balance independently reviewable. Do not copy manuals, worksheets, scripts, or training materials.
reviewerNotes: Approved by Dustin Rowland. In the slice-of-life/question-bank model, selecting a specific therapy modality means recommending it now. The game does not benefit from simulating an adequate future trial, protocol, duration, or completion. Source/article and diagnosis records may still preserve language such as a full course of DBT, but encounter data and point rules need only the therapy type. Prior psychotherapy trials remain separate patient history and are revealed through the existing full psychiatric treatment-history action.
resurfacingTrigger: Only if a future focused encounter genuinely makes delivery form, course completion, or program fidelity part of the immediate best-next-step decision.

resolution.note: Preserved the existing stable TreatmentOption ID as the encounter modality identity, split the aggregate catalog into one file per reusable treatment or disposition, added exact registry membership validation, and documented that submitted treatment and scoring contain only intervention IDs. Historical psychotherapy trials remain independently structured under full treatment history. No delivery scope, fidelity, duration, completion, clinical mapping, point value, or runtime behavior was added.

title: Stage common outpatient diagnosis identities without inventing criteria
proposedRouting: Add neutral identities only after deciding family granularity, then create separate tickets for criteria, focused actions, compatibility, treatment mappings, and balance.
guidance: The existing requested case families already have stable definitions. The clearest next identity gaps are panic disorder, social anxiety disorder, obsessive-compulsive disorder, ADHD, insomnia disorder, and adjustment disorder. Alcohol- and opioid-use disorders need a separate family-granularity decision because their treatment pathways differ. ICD-10-CM can support authoring search and NIMH can supply broad public-domain context, but neither silently supplies executable diagnostic criteria or treatment rules. Cyclothymia remains under its dedicated duration/source ticket.
resurfacingTrigger: Before adding a case from one of these families or exposing its treatment options.

title: Model medication regimen benefit, risk, and duplication
proposedRouting: Create an authoring-only, point-free medication-regimen catalog with explicit class memberships, concrete start and entry-targeted operations, route-owned transition meaning, and separately typed qualitative contributors. Never derive a class, duplicate, interaction, or penalty from free-text class labels, tags, medication count, or file order.
guidance: The player submits starts and entry-targeted continue, increase, reduce_or_limit, taper, or stop operations only. A focused reviewed diagnosis route or decision policy owns the acceptable transition shape and explains it as initial treatment, replacement, augmentation, simplification, or maintenance/optimization. Benefit, response, tolerability, prior-trial, fit, duplication, interaction, withdrawal, contraindication, and prerequisite contributors remain separately traceable and point-free. A replacement-shaped start plus taper/stop never implies safe overlap, washout, or cross-taper timing. No blanket same-class penalty or universal regimen-quality score is permitted.
reviewerNotes: Approved by Dustin Rowland. Concrete regimen operations remain the player input; the focused reviewed route owns transition meaning. The model must scale from one initial first-line start to retaining a beneficial anchor, reducing or stopping a poor-fit entry, and adding an eligible adjunct. Unmatched but plausible plans remain engine-inferred. Do not add a player intent field, dose or schedule mechanics, predicted outcomes, automatic clinical winner, blanket class penalty, or points from this architecture decision.
resurfacingTrigger: When adding the first reviewed medication class, membership, focused route, qualitative regimen contributor, pair-specific transition safety rule, or balance mapping.

resolution.note: Added a runtime-excluded, empty medication-regimen knowledge catalog and strict schemas for explicit classes/memberships, concrete V2 starts and entry-targeted adjustments, route-owned explanatory meaning, and separate qualitative contributors. Added reference validation for regimen entries, medication/class versions, provenance, and registry membership. No clinical relationship, class membership, route, point value, compatibility-case score, cross-taper rule, or medical approval was activated. Existing rule-provenance and medication-allowlist work remains separate.

title: Define the RxClass relation-source allowlist
proposedRouting: Create the smallest per-relation-source rights map and explicit importer allowlist before storing any RxClass class or membership relationship.
guidance: RxClass aggregates independently governed sources. Quarantine SNOMED CT and WHO ATC or ATCPROD until separately licensed or cleared. Preserve relation source, source version, relation type, class ID and type, RxCUI, member term type, and direct or indirect state. Never blend competing sources or infer a PsychSim indication, contraindication, class, rule, or point value from the API relationship alone.
resurfacingTrigger: Before any RxClass API call is materialized into a medication, class, relationship, rule, or runtime record.

title: Define a safe DailyMed metadata and label-version boundary
proposedRouting: Decide whether a narrow factual DailyMed metadata subset can receive a separate source-use decision while company-submitted label prose and media remain excluded.
guidance: Review SET ID, version, update time, active or archive state, application number, RxCUI, NDC, labeler, and product name independently from SPL prose, PDF or XML content, images, and media. Prefer openFDA's explicitly Public Domain and CC0-labeled dataset for the first protected label-assertion proof. A public API is not itself permission to transform every returned field.
resurfacingTrigger: Before any DailyMed response or download is stored, indexed, sent to AI, adapted, or exposed in a distributed artifact.

title: Make assertion and third-party clearance machine-readable
proposedRouting: Extend a formal contribution with a constrained assertion kind and per-source material-clearance record before any narrow aggregate or terminology source can support more than its current allowlisted contribution lanes.
guidance: Allowed contribution types are now machine-enforced, so MeSH and FDA CYP data cannot silently become treatment, safety, or scoring support and openFDA remains context/teaching-only. The remaining technical gap is finer than a contribution type: a future record must distinguish terminology mapping, source-authored factual assertion, interaction hypothesis, contraindication, recommendation, monitoring rule, and point rule, and must state whether item-level third-party material was excluded or independently cleared. Design this as a constrained union, not prose parsing or a general expression language. Until then, do not widen the narrow allowlists.
resurfacingTrigger: Before widening an allowed contribution type for MeSH, LactMed, LiverTox, FDA CYP examples, openFDA labels, or another mixed-source aggregate.

title: Source background medication and supplement generation
proposedRouting: Find representative utilization data, then separately review age bands, medication and supplement count envelopes, neutral-background allowlists, and the optional multi-supplement pattern before any generator is activated.
guidance: The generated patient may eventually resolve nonpsychiatric medications and supplements before reveal, with more background medication burden possible at older ages. Population estimates, reviewed identity allowlists, deterministic game calibration, and clinically meaningful impact classification must remain separate. The supplement-enthusiast pattern is an internal diversity mechanism, not a diagnosis or stereotype. This ticket authorizes no probability, count, allowlist, generated exposure, patient fact, or rule.
resurfacingTrigger: Before activating any age-dependent background medication or supplement generator, count distribution, allowlist, or supplement-enthusiast frequency.

title: Source effects and interactions for initial supplements
proposedRouting: Keep all six entries identity-only while preparation-specific evidence questions are identified. Split any proposed psychiatric effect, adverse effect, interaction, or safety assertion into an exact claim with its own provenance and clinical review before activation.
guidance: MeSH and RxNorm support identity only. They do not establish efficacy, safety, interaction severity, dosing, preparation equivalence, patient-level prevalence, generation probability, treatment availability, or points. Whole botanicals, extracts, essential oils, routes, and standardized products must not be treated as interchangeable. This ticket authorizes no clinical claim or runtime behavior.
resurfacingTrigger: Before changing any initial supplement from neutral identity metadata to fit-relevant, safety-relevant, case-defining, selectable, or scored content.

title: Source current-regimen adjustment operations
proposedRouting: Define continue, increase, reduce or limit, taper, and stop as regimen-entry-targeted snapshot operations, then source medication- or class-specific withdrawal, toxicity, duplication, and transition boundaries before any operation is graded.
guidance: The operation vocabulary makes duplicate prescriptions independently addressable and supports focused polypharmacy decisions without simulating a schedule. It does not establish that a particular medication can be stopped abruptly, how it should be tapered, whether a dose should be increased, or how two operations should interact. Those remain exact, source-linked rules with separate point review.
resurfacingTrigger: Before wiring regimen-entry operations into treatment selection or grading any continue, increase, reduce or limit, taper, or stop choice.

title: Design a focused polypharmacy-cleanup patient family
proposedRouting: After regimen-entry operations and source-linked withdrawal boundaries exist, author one focused snapshot whose broad path is parsimonious cleanup while the engine separately traces duplicate therapy, likely nonbenefit, interaction burden, withdrawal risk, and each selected adjustment.
guidance: The case should ask for the best next medication-regimen decision, not a comprehensive reconstruction of every diagnosis or a longitudinal taper schedule. It needs at least one safe broad path, independently addressable duplicate entries, objective current-benefit and tolerability facts, and a receipt that prevents the same underlying regimen problem from receiving stacked duplicate penalties.
resurfacingTrigger: After regimen-entry operations and at least one source-reviewed withdrawal or duplicate-therapy rule are executable.

title: Design a focused delirium-with-polypharmacy patient family
proposedRouting: Keep delirium explicit and case-defining. After a legally processable source and regimen-operation rules exist, author one hospital or consultation snapshot that asks which immediate medication burden to reduce or stop and which medical evaluation or disposition takes priority.
guidance: Delirium must not appear as an incidental random diagnosis. The patient may carry a large medication list, but the encounter still grades a focused best next step rather than demanding a complete nine-medication plan. The case must preserve withdrawal hazards, toxicity, duplicate therapy, active benefit, and safe escalation as separate traceable contributors.
resurfacingTrigger: When a delirium source is legally processable and the regimen-operation model can support a safe focused hospital or consultation case.

title: Separate persistent depressive disorder from MDD
proposedRouting: Keep the new persistent-depressive-disorder record identity-only while a reviewed source packet defines its longitudinal boundary and relationship to MDD.
guidance: The runtime catalog now has a neutral, medically unreviewed identity for persistent depressive disorder (dysthymia). It has no criteria, duration, severity, compatibility, treatment, or scoring behavior. Review the current diagnostic naming, the relationship among persistent subthreshold symptoms, chronic major depressive episodes, and partial remission, and whether one or more patient families are useful for a focused question-bank snapshot. Do not model persistent depressive disorder as an MDD severity level or infer it from prose duration before the boundary is source-reviewed.
resurfacingTrigger: Before adding criteria, a duration generator, an MDD compatibility rule, a patient family, or treatment behavior for persistent depressive disorder.

title: Review BPD versus bipolar differentiation sources
proposedRouting: Review each identified private note as its own hash-bound private packet, independently verify its cited publication, and then split context, differential findings, and Developer interpretation into separate proposals.
guidance: The private corpus contains separate candidates about diagnostic medicalization, latent-factor overlap, and possible differentiating findings. They are currently lexical retrieval records, not evidence or clinical claims. OCR attachment text remains outside the authorized semantic boundary, and the APA BPD guideline remains treatment-only and blocked from AI processing. Prepare one complete private source revision at a time; do not flatten the notes into one conclusion or treat affective instability, self-harm, or ordinary mood variation as a diagnosis. Any later differential rule must preserve uncertainty, longitudinal context, source applicability, and a distinct Developer-opinion lane.
resurfacingTrigger: When a private BPD/bipolar packet is prepared, a reusable diagnostic source is cleared, or a differential patient family is proposed.

title: Define the alcohol-withdrawal diagnosis family
proposedRouting: Use classification terms for identity lookup only, then source and review the smallest diagnosis-family split needed for a focused ED snapshot.
guidance: The authoring-only ICD-10-CM catalog distinguishes alcohol withdrawal without delirium from withdrawal delirium, but it supplies no executable criteria, severity logic, or treatment. Decide whether alcohol use disorder, acute withdrawal, perceptual disturbance, seizure risk, and alcohol-withdrawal delirium require separate internal condition states or reviewed qualifiers. The label “DTs” must not become a generic synonym for any withdrawal state. No diagnosis file, compatibility relation, patient generation, or score is authorized by this ticket.
resurfacingTrigger: Before adding any alcohol-withdrawal diagnosis definition, patient state, compatibility rule, or case family.

title: Separate alcohol-withdrawal assessment instruments
proposedRouting: Create separate proposed instrument identities only after verifying each full name, owner, version, setting, scoring semantics, and reproduction rights.
guidance: CIWA-Ar, MAWS, MINDS, and modified MINDS are not aliases for one interchangeable scale or protocol. A local note mentioning an acronym establishes only that the term appeared in a workflow; it does not establish the instrument identity, validity, threshold, treatment protocol, or right to reproduce its items. Preserve each proposed identity separately, and keep institution-specific order sets or medication algorithms distinct from the assessment instrument itself. Do not add exact item text, score interpretation, treatment triggers, or gameplay behavior until version and rights review is complete.
resurfacingTrigger: Before adding an alcohol-withdrawal scale to the investigation catalog, displaying a score, or grading an instrument-driven action.

title: Design a focused ED alcohol-withdrawal snapshot
proposedRouting: After diagnosis, instrument, acute-medication, and disposition boundaries are reviewed, author one ED best-next-step snapshot with at least one complete safe route.
guidance: Keep this as a short question-bank decision rather than an alcohol-withdrawal simulator. The later patient may ask the player to recognize escalation, choose a focused workup, select one immediate intervention family, and choose disposition. It must distinguish withdrawal delirium from uncomplicated withdrawal, preserve medication and monitoring constraints, and avoid importing a local institutional protocol as general guidance. Do not add a playable case until an Emergency Department exists and validation can prove an accessible safe workup, intervention, and disposition.
resurfacingTrigger: When the ED department exists and source-reviewed alcohol-withdrawal diagnosis, assessment, acute-treatment, and disposition boundaries are available.

title: Bound hypothyroidism presenting as depression
proposedRouting: Source the medical-condition and laboratory boundary first, then consider one focused recognition-and-referral snapshot without simulating endocrine management.
guidance: Current content supports targeted TSH ordering but not a case in which hypothyroidism is the case-defining explanation. A later snapshot needs a reviewed medical-condition identity, an authored nonincidental laboratory pattern, appropriate history or examination clues, a free-thyroxine boundary if needed, and a safe medical-coordination or referral path. It must not convert a bounded incidental TSH flag into a diagnosis or require thyroid testing in every depressive presentation. No laboratory pattern, diagnosis, treatment, disposition, or point behavior is authorized here.
resurfacingTrigger: Before adding a hypothyroidism condition identity, free-thyroxine test, case-defining thyroid result, or depressive-presentation patient family.

title: Make chief-complaint pool inheritance explicit
proposedRouting: Add an explicit, validated complaint-pool composition and inheritance record before derived patient families reuse presentation text.
guidance: Current scenarios each own at least ten complaint strings, and the queue avoids exact recently used strings, but there is no shared pool identity, inheritance provenance, semantic-cluster deduplication, or diagnosis-hint validator. A later compiler should record whether a patient family inherits, composes, or overrides neutral complaint fragments; preserve misleading and cross-diagnostic complaints where intentionally reviewed; reject hidden case labels or pathway names; and keep the resolved complaint saved for replay. Do not make a diagnosis file the automatic wording owner, because that can turn the launcher into an answer key.
resurfacingTrigger: Before adding reusable chief-complaint catalogs, derived patient-template inheritance, semantic recent-use suppression, or new patient families at scale.

title: Define broad and unspecified diagnosis-answer credit
proposedRouting: Add an explicit versioned diagnosis hierarchy, real broad and unspecified catalog entries, and deterministic hierarchy-aware answer matching before scaling diagnosis scoring beyond case-authored options.
guidance: A player may submit no diagnosis, a broad category, an unspecified diagnosis, or a more specific supported diagnosis. Blank remains a valid submission and receives only the case-authored omission consequence. A correctly matched broad family or unspecified diagnosis should receive meaningful partial credit; a supported specific diagnosis may receive more; an unrelated family receives no positive credit and may receive a case-specific misclassification consequence when it would materially change management. Do not infer ancestry from label text, ICD prefixes, file order, or free tags. The hierarchy owns identity and ancestry only; each focused patient rubric still owns point magnitudes, reasonable alternatives, dangerous confusions, and whether added specificity is actually supported by revealed facts.
resurfacingTrigger: Before adding broad or unspecified diagnosis choices to runtime menus, applying catalog-derived partial credit, or scaling diagnosis answer scoring to another patient family.
